descr.name: Inhibition of Lassa virus GPC expressed in recombinant vaccinia virus infected in African green monkey Vero cells assessed as reduction in GPC-mediated cell-cell fusion by beta-galactosidase reporter gene assay
description: Title: SAR studies of 4-acyl-1,6-dialkylpiperazin-2-one arenavirus cell entry inhibitors.

Abstract: Old World (Africa) and New World (South America) arenaviruses are associated with human hemorrhagic fevers. Efforts to develop small molecule therapeutics have yielded several chemical series including the 4-acyl-1,6-dialkylpiperazin-2-ones. Herein, we describe an extensive exploration of this chemotype. In initial Phase I studies, R<sup>1</sup> and R<sup>4</sup> scanning libraries were assayed to identify potent substituents against Old World (Lassa) virus. In subsequent Phase II studies, R<sup>6</sup> substituents and iterative R<sup>1</sup>, R<sup>4</sup> and R<sup>6</sup> substituent combinations were evaluated to obtain compounds with improved Lassa and New World (Machupo, Junin, and Tacaribe) arenavirus inhibitory activity, in vitro human liver microsome metabolic stability and aqueous solubility.
comment: Compounds with activity <= 10uM or explicitly reported as active by ChEMBL are flagged as active in this PubChem assay presentation.
